title.en: "Who is this?" failing for two different reasons was answered as though it were one.

summary.en: Resolving a person fails because the name is nobody's — the caller's input is wrong — or because the user store could not be read, which is the server's fault.

title.en: An order could be placed in anybody's name.
title.de: An order could be placed in anybody's name.

summary.en: HandlePlace took the recipient straight out of the request body and asked nothing about it, so any account that could reach a catalogue could put an order — and an approval in that person's manager's inbox, a line in their record, and eventually a provisioning run — in a colleague's name.

title.en: The recipient of an order is picked, not typed — and the field is only shown to accounts that may use it.

summary.en: Ordering in somebody else's name became a first-class screen gated on the operator role, and the field it goes through took a free string and offered no help finding one.

title.en: A catalogue can be searched, and by words it does not display.

summary.en: The portal browsed and did not find.

title.en: The approval list can be searched and ordered.

summary.en: It rendered every open approval in whatever order the endpoint returned — newest first — which is fine at three and a wall at forty.

title.en: Two pages rendered the literal word "null".

title.en: The catalogue can now be read backwards.

summary.en: Every question it answered ran forwards: a product names what it contains, what it needs, what it excludes.

title.en: Products can be marked as favourites.

summary.en: The smallest measure in the plan, and the one whose two decisions are the kind that get made by accident.

title.en: A product can now say who may receive it.
title.de: A product can now say who may receive it.

summary.en: A catalogue carries an audience and that gate is fail-closed — but it was the only gate: whoever was in a catalogue's audience could order anything in it, and the sole thing between a person and domain administration was an approval rule, which says who decides rather than who may ask.

title.en: A hold that ends now leaves a record that it existed.
title.de: A hold that ends now leaves a record that it existed.

summary.en: The inventory is present tense by construction — a grant writes a row, a revocation deletes it — and the order behind a right is deleted by retention long before the right ends, which is why the inventory is engine state at all.

title.en: The catalogue can now say what must never be held together.

summary.en: Everything the portal had learned about access was detective or temporal: the commissioning load records what was there, reconciliation checks whether the record is true, recertification asks whether it is justified, an expiry ends it by itself.

title.en: A reminder can now ask what is waiting for somebody else.

summary.en: The portal asks people for three different things — decide an order line, answer a recertification row, do a task — and none of it happens while nobody opens Atlas and looks.
